youtube_title: White River Light Station: footsteps on the stairs and the keeper of more than 40 years
body: Footsteps on the stairs in the middle of the night: that's what a former curator reported at the White River Light Station, near Whitehall, Michigan. The lighthouse was built in 1875 and first lit in May 1876. Its first keeper was Captain William Robinson, who came from England. He and his wife, Sarah, had 13 children, and he kept the light for more than 40 years. In 1919, at 87, he was retired, and his grandson took over as keeper; that same spring, the old captain died. People say he never left. Guests and staff have reported footsteps upstairs and the tap of a cane. The light was shut off in 1960, and since 1970 it has been a museum, open in season. 👻 Comment your town, and it could be next! #Whitehall #WhiteRiverLight #Michigan #Lighthouse #LakeMichigan #Haunted #LaPorteAfterDark
